summary:
Jenna Kutcher, former wedding photographer turned digital entrepreneur who hosted the Gold Digger podcast for 968 episodes and wrote a New York Times bestselling book, discusses Pinterest strategy for Etsy sellers with Dylan Jahraus. She explains that Pinterest functions as a quiet system running in the background that sends tens of thousands of visitors to her site monthly with approximately one hour of weekly work. The platform requires no engaging, no showing your face, and content continues working for months or years rather than dying within hours like Instagram posts.

The interview establishes specific metrics comparing platforms: Instagram posts have a 24-48 hour shelf life while Pinterest pins have a 13+ month half-life. Dylan shows her Etsy traffic dashboard where Pinterest drove 552,000 visits despite spending 10-20 times more effort on Facebook. Jenna notes that 96% of Pinterest searches are unbranded, meaning users are actively open to discovering new sellers rather than searching for specific brands.

Jenna outlines the practical implementation: the system takes one hour per week versus the average entrepreneur's 19-20 hours on marketing. Users should post one to two fresh pins daily, which can all be scheduled in one weekly session. Fresh pins don't require new products - creators can make 5-10 or even 20 different pins for a single product or piece of content by varying designs and titles. The strategy can be fully outsourced to a virtual assistant at typical rates of $30-35 per hour.

For declining traffic, Jenna identifies two causes: pins not being differentiated enough to count as fresh, or keywords not matching actual search terms. She emphasizes that boards should be titled around how people actually search (specific terms like 'living room wall art') rather than creative or cheeky names. For products, lifestyle mockups showing items in use outperform sterile white backgrounds. For digital products getting views but not clicks, she advises focusing on outcomes rather than features - instead of 'social media plan PDF', use 'plan a month of content in 30 minutes'.

The discussion covers technical details: Pinterest pins now rank in Google search results, Etsy listing URLs work directly as pin destinations without needing a separate website, and users can pin to multiple platforms including Shopify, Etsy, personal websites, and even use Pinterest to grow Instagram following. Results typically appear within 30-60 days of consistent implementation.

Jenna announces her upcoming five-day Pinterest boot camp starting January 25th, priced at $27, featuring 15-minute daily live sessions plus Q&A, with replays available for 10 days. The boot camp includes an AI assistant built as a GPT to walk through daily assignments. She cites student SK Carr who achieved over one million Pinterest views within 60 days of starting after completing the June boot camp. The boot camp covers profile setup, content type selection based on business type, keyword research to validate product ideas, and leveraging existing content.
